correctness.rationale: For every RC-closed nonoverlapping code, first-symbol set P is disjoint from complement P and embeds in a complementary transversal. Complement-preserving symbol permutations map it to {A,C}; all candidates lie in 256 canonical words. At length five RC has no fixed words. Exhaustive lexicographic orbit generation yields 56 internally valid pairs and 412 exact conflicting pair edges. The included 18 explicit blocks partition the vertices into cliques, proving every compatible independent set has <=18 vertices and thus <=36 words; the explicit 18-orbit witness has 36 pairwise nonoverlapping words. Both standard-library scripts recompute all critical comparisons using separately implemented character and integer algorithms and pass.

A size-24 maximum in a subset does not determine a maximum in its superset, especially when the new 36-word witness may use unbalanced words.

value.rationale: Determines the exact five-base capacity of DNA frame synchronization tokens required to work in both Watson–Crick strand orientations, using a succinct independently checkable 18-clique certificate. It is the first odd-length setting beyond three and has no fixed RC orbits, a concrete structural change from the adjacent four-mer problem. It quantifies the 36 versus 81 cardinality gap relative to unconstrained coding and supplies a reproducible 36-token construction; the natural biological alphabet, orientation closure, and fixed five-base length motivate the exact invariant. No claim of a larger-length theorem or biochemical validation is made.
